config.title: useTransition

intro.title: useTransition
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build a simple toggle component that smoothly fades between two text states using Vue's useTransition hook. You'll learn how useTransition manages animated state changes by tracking pending transitions and providing timing controls. The main technologies involved are Vue 3's Composition API, the useTransition hook, and CSS transitions. This beginner-friendly lesson will show you how to create smooth UI animations while maintaining responsive user interactions.
intro.usecase: Vue's useTransition is essential for creating polished, professional interfaces where smooth animations enhance user experience. Developers implement this pattern in dashboard applications when showing/hiding data panels, in e-commerce sites for cart slide-ins and product detail transitions, and in admin interfaces for modal dialogs and expanding filter sections. This API allows you to control enter/leave animations for elements that conditionally render, making UI interactions feel responsive and intentional. Mastering useTransition helps you build applications that meet modern user expectations for fluid, engaging interfaces.

objectives: Initialize a transition state using the useTransition hook
Configure transition modes to control element behavior during animations
Bind transition states to template elements for visual feedback
Implement conditional rendering with smooth transition effects
Manipulate transition timing and easing for customized animations
Integrate transition hooks with reactive data for dynamic UI updates
Control transition phases (enter/leave) to manage animation sequences

steps.title: Add CSS transitions
steps.instruction: Add a <style> section at the end of your Vue component with CSS classes for enter and leave transitions. Include a .fade-enter-active class with transition: opacity 0.5s ease; and a .fade-leave-active class with transition: opacity 0.5s ease;.
steps.hint: The <style> tag goes after the closing </template> tag. You can define CSS classes that Vue's transition system will automatically apply during enter/leave animations.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have CSS transition styles that Vue can use to animate the enter/leave transitions.
successCriteria: A <style> section is added with .fade-enter-active and .fade-leave-active classes containing transition properties.
